messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Reason for Admission:
The patient was admitted to the hospital for treatment of HIV infection.

Hospital Course:
During the admission, the patient was started on ART, and 186 SMS text messages were sent and received to remind her to take medication. The patient responded to only 28% of the text messages and did not respond to the remaining 72%. During feedback sessions, the patient claimed to have taken medication as per the instructions given and responded to all the text messages. Later, during an interview, the patient disclosed that she was not honest during the feedback sessions as she was depressed about unwanted disclosure of her HIV status and stigma related to HIV. She also mentioned that she deletes the SMS text messages once she replies to them to avoid any possible disclosure of her status.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Discharge Condition:
The patient will be discharged once her treatment is completed.

Discharge Instructions:
The patient is instructed to continue with ART medication as per the instructions given by the healthcare provider. The patient is also advised to follow up with the healthcare provider as per the scheduled appointments and to disclose any concerns or issues related to her treatment. The patient is also requested to maintain the confidentiality of her HIV status and not to reveal it to anyone without proper authorization. 

Signatures:
The discharge summary was dictated by the healthcare provider and reviewed and approved by the medical transcriptionist.

Dictated by: Dr. Sample
Reviewed by: John Doe, MT

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The patient was admitted to start ART for HIV infection, so HIV disease is chiefly responsible for the episode. Her depression and poor adherence are secondary issues, not the reason for admission. No specific HIV-related manifestation is documented, so this is unspecified HIV disease in chapter B, category B24.

CODE: B24
